title: Beyond the Chatbox: Running Real ML in the Browser
abstract: Large models are not the only way to use AI. We run pose estimation, embeddings and OCR entirely client-side with WebGPU and wasm — no server round-trip, no data leaving the device.

title: WebGPU for the Rest of Us
abstract: A gentle tour of the WebGPU API: adapters, devices, compute shaders and buffers. We build a tiny matrix-multiply kernel and watch it run on the GPU straight from JavaScript.

title: Tiny Transformers, Big Impact
abstract: Distilled sentence-embedding models are only a few megabytes yet power semantic search, clustering and recommendations. We benchmark them against their heavyweight cousins.

title: Taking Care of Yourself: Wellbeing and Burnout in Tech
abstract: A candid talk on exhaustion, recognizing when you are unwell, taking time off to recover without guilt, and building teams that protect the health of their engineers.

title: Semantic Search Without a Vector Database
abstract: For thousands of documents you do not need a cluster. Compute embeddings once, keep them in memory, and rank with cosine similarity in a few lines of code.

title: Signals All the Way Down: Reactive Angular in 2026
abstract: Angular's signals turn change detection inside out. We refactor a jittery component tree into fine-grained reactive state and delete our last RxJS subscription.

title: Kotlin Coroutines Under the Hood
abstract: Suspend functions look like magic. We disassemble the continuation-passing transformation the compiler performs and demystify structured concurrency.

title: Spring Boot 4: What Actually Changed
abstract: Renamed starters, Jackson 3, a new baseline JDK. A pragmatic migration guide for teams moving off the end-of-life 3.x line without rewriting the world.

title: OCR in the Browser with Tesseract.js
abstract: Turn a webcam frame into editable text on-device. We cover image preprocessing, language data, and why a threshold pass doubles recognition accuracy.

title: The Privacy Dividend of On-Device Inference
abstract: When the model runs locally, sensitive data never travels. We quantify the latency, cost and trust benefits of keeping inference on the client.

title: Quantization Demystified
abstract: int8, float16, q4 — what do they cost and what do they save? We measure accuracy and speed trade-offs on a laptop GPU and a phone.

title: Web Workers Are Your Friend
abstract: Keep the main thread buttery smooth by moving heavy computation off it. Message passing, transferable objects, and module workers explained with live demos.

title: Designing for the Colour-Blind
abstract: Roughly one in twelve men cannot distinguish your red-green status badges. Practical palette choices, contrast ratios and testing tools for accessible UI.

title: From REST to gRPC and Back Again
abstract: We migrated a fleet of services to gRPC, hit real-world pain, and returned to JSON over HTTP for the public edge. Lessons on protocol choice.

title: Testing the Untestable: ML in CI
abstract: Model outputs are fuzzy, so exact-match assertions fail. We show tolerance-based checks, fixed seeds, and golden-file strategies for reliable pipelines.

title: The Art of the Live Demo
abstract: Everything that can go wrong on stage will. Offline-first assets, warm caches, fallback backends and a calm HUD that shows the machinery working.

title: Cosine Similarity Is All You Need
abstract: A surprisingly deep look at the humblest metric in machine learning: why normalized dot products capture meaning, and where they quietly mislead you.

title: Streaming Tokens: Building a Chat UI That Feels Fast
abstract: Perceived latency beats real latency. Skeletons, optimistic rendering and token streaming make a slow model feel instant to your users.

title: The Case for Boring Databases
abstract: Postgres can do full-text search, JSON, queues and even vectors. Before you add a new datastore, see how far one boring database will carry you.

title: Edge AI on a Ten-Dollar Microcontroller
abstract: Keyword spotting and gesture recognition on hardware with kilobytes of RAM. We squeeze a neural net into a coin-cell-powered board.

title: Feature Flags Without the Footguns
abstract: Flags let you ship on Friday, but stale flags rot your codebase. A discipline for creating, measuring and — crucially — deleting them.

title: Rendering a Million Points at Sixty FPS
abstract: Canvas, WebGL and WebGPU compared for large scatter plots. Instancing, level-of-detail and off-thread layout keep interaction crisp.

title: Prompt Injection Is the New SQL Injection
abstract: Untrusted text reaching a model is an attack surface. We taxonomize injection techniques and the defensive boundaries that actually hold.

title: The Zen of Zoneless Angular
abstract: Dropping zone.js shrinks the bundle and sharpens change detection. We walk through the migration and the mental model that replaces it.

title: Type-Safe Forms That Users Actually Enjoy
abstract: Strictly typed reactive forms catch bugs at compile time and guide validation. We build a multi-step form with zero runtime type surprises.

title: Observability for the Anxious Engineer
abstract: Logs, metrics and traces without drowning in dashboards. What to instrument first, and how to sleep through the night on call.

title: The Hidden Cost of node_modules
abstract: Supply-chain risk, install time and disk churn. We audit a real project's dependency tree and cut it in half without losing features.

title: Letterboxing, Padding and Other Preprocessing Sins
abstract: Garbage in, garbage out: how sloppy image resizing wrecks model accuracy, and the aspect-ratio-preserving pipeline that fixes it.

title: A Field Guide to Floating Point
abstract: Why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3, how NaN propagates, and the rounding modes that bite numerical code. Practical defenses for everyday developers.

title: Progressive Web Apps Are Back
abstract: Installable, offline-capable, push-enabled. Service workers and the cache API turn a website into an app your users keep on their home screen.

title: Cold Starts and Warm Predictors
abstract: A model that loads lazily ruins the first request. We preload weights, warm the inference session at startup, and log the warmup so we trust it.

title: Explainable Recommendations
abstract: Nearest-neighbour search gives you 'why' for free: show the items that pulled a result up. Users trust recommendations they can interrogate.

title: Camera, Canvas, Compute: The Browser Vision Stack
abstract: From getUserMedia to a tensor on the GPU. We assemble a full webcam-to-inference pipeline and handle every permission and fallback along the way.

title: Debugging WebAssembly Without Losing Your Mind
abstract: Source maps, DWARF symbols and console.log across the JS/wasm boundary. Tooling that turns opaque crashes into readable stack traces.

title: Rate Limiting, Backpressure and Graceful Degradation
abstract: When traffic spikes, fail politely. Token buckets, queue depth signals and the art of shedding load before it sheds you.

title: The Multilingual Web
abstract: Internationalization is more than string tables: pluralization, right-to-left layout, and models that understand more than English.

title: Small Data, Big Models, Careful Fine-Tuning
abstract: You rarely need to train from scratch. Adapters and a few hundred labelled examples specialize a base model to your domain cheaply.

title: Immutable by Default
abstract: Val over var, copy over mutate. How a bias toward immutability in Kotlin and TypeScript eliminates a whole class of concurrency bugs.

title: The Accessibility Tree Is an API
abstract: Screen readers consume a structured tree your markup generates. Learn to inspect it, test it, and stop shipping invisible buttons.

title: Vectorizing Your Documentation
abstract: Turn a wiki into a searchable knowledge base with embeddings. Chunking strategies, overlap, and keeping the index fresh as docs change.

title: GPU Memory Is Not Infinite
abstract: Manual tensor lifetimes, buffer reuse and the readback trap. Practical patterns to avoid leaks and out-of-memory crashes in browser ML.

title: The Ergonomics of Error Handling
abstract: Result types, exceptions and the messages your future self will read at 3am. Designing failures that explain themselves.

title: Benchmarking Honestly
abstract: Warmup runs, percentiles not averages, and controlling for thermal throttling. How to publish numbers you will not have to retract.

title: From Notebook to Production
abstract: The messy path from a data scientist's experiment to a service with SLAs. Packaging weights, pinning versions and reproducible builds.

title: Dark Mode Is a Design System Problem
abstract: Two themes double your surface area. Semantic colour tokens, contrast testing and a single source of truth keep both palettes honest.

title: The Long Tail of Browser Compatibility
abstract: WebGPU is not everywhere yet. Feature detection, wasm fallbacks and honest UI badges so users on older machines still get a working app.

title: Caching Is the Hardest Problem
abstract: Invalidation, staleness and the thundering herd. Strategies from HTTP headers to service workers to keep fast things fast and correct.

title: Ethics of Ambient AI
abstract: Always-on cameras and microphones raise hard questions. Consent, on-device processing and data minimization as first-class design constraints.

title: Reproducible Builds for ML Assets
abstract: Pin every model URL and checksum so a build is byte-for-byte repeatable and offline-safe. A download script that fails loudly on drift.

title: The Joy of Deleting Code
abstract: The best pull request is often a red one. How to find dead paths, retire features safely, and celebrate the lines you remove.
